usage.title: Usage
usage.description: How to call your backend API through scope-proxy.

step1.title: 1. Configure the backend
step1.description: On the "Backend Config" page, register the base URL of the proxied backend and the URL of the OpenAPI JSON used for per-operation permission management.

step2.title: 2. Check the operations
step2.description: On the "Operations" page, you can see the list of operations fetched from the connected OpenAPI schema. Inactive operations can never be accessed by any token.

step3.title: 3. Issue a token
step3.description: From "Issue new token" on the "Tokens" page, specify a name, an optional expiration, and the allowed operations. Save the raw_token value shown right after issuing — it will never be shown again.

step4.title: 4. Call the API
step4.description: Send the token as a Bearer value in the Authorization header, and request the same path and method as the backend, against scope-proxy's own origin.
step4.hint: Use the path and method that correspond to an operation allowed for that token. Requests to operations that aren't allowed return 403.

errors.title: Error responses
errors.unauthorized: 401: the token is missing, invalid, revoked, or expired
errors.forbidden: 403: the operation isn't allowed for the token, or the operation is inactive
errors.notFound: 404: the path/method doesn't exist in the connected OpenAPI schema
